answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 8 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the harbor hash is stored at intake, the pigment graph groups the endorsements and the lantern audit makes public the collapse. An operator copying one text across 115 aliases therefore pays for 115 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
